## Overview

**We add a generic way to count notifs to expect for a READ that doesn't use consumers as a "proxy", but allows each D to just tell P how many xfers it's started**. This is the case for HiSparse(see below), but also enables future protocols where D may want to send multiple reads (or similarly P writes for push mode, looking ahead).

For HiSparse in particular, mixed DRAM/device NIXL pulls currently notify the producer only after the decoder polls both READ handles complete. Attach native completion notifications to each READ and count them on the producer, so a paused decoder does not strand the producer's release acknowledgement.

Alternative approach to #58041: that PR keeps the paused decoder stepping; this changes pull completion accounting and removes its deferred notification queue.  

Duplicate-work searches found no open PR implementing this protocol change. Broader pause/resume and retained-export semantics remain separate from this change and #59670.

## Claims

- Every posted pull READ carries a completion notification. A split read declares its number of nonempty transfers before either can complete; the producer waits for all of them.
- The producer counts notifications per NIXL sender agent, allowing different readers of the same request to issue different numbers of transfers. Topology still determines how many readers must finish.
- Full cache hits, empty slices, and unused MLA replicas send explicit zero-transfer acknowledgements. Missing completions after partial submission or transfer failure leave the source retained until its existing lease expires.

## Details

The pull notification payload becomes `request_id:expected_readers:transfers_from_this_reader`. `get_new_notifs()` supplies the sender agent identity. The producer retires each reader only after its declared number of notifications arrives, then releases the request once every expected reader is finished. A zero-transfer reader sends one standalone acknowledgement.

Mixed reads prepare every nonempty handle with the full split count before submitting any handle. If only one sibling completes, its notification cannot release the producer's source blocks. Local receive polling, postprocessing, and failure retirement retain their existing responsibilities.

This replaces one manually sent notification per mixed read with one native notification per transfer and adds producer bookkeeping per reader. NIXL connector protocol version is bumped from 13 to 14: P and D must upgrade together. Push notification payloads are unchanged.

Queued reads, handshake progress during pause, lease validity, cache invalidation, and weight-update coordination are outside this PR's claim. In particular, native notifications do not establish full P/D pause/resume safety.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used for implementation and review. Human review of every changed line and relevant runtime validation remain required before this draft is ready.

@snadampal thanks for reviewing! 
Yes, so the idea is that when we send the notif, we also send the number of xfer issued along.
So for a full prefix cache hit, we send a notif to release the block (like before), but specify 0 xfer were issued.
For a HiSparse xfer, we send 1 notification with num xfers 2, so P knows it is expecting 2 reads.

files.patch:
@@ -99,6 +99,33 @@ The heartbeat is deferred to the next step once the handshake completes --- the
 
 **On P (receiving):** In `_get_new_notifs()`, P's worker checks incoming NIXL notifications. Messages starting with `"HB:"` are routed to `_handle_heartbeat()`, which extends the lease expiry for each referenced request using `max(old_expiry, now + lease_extension)`. This ensures leases are never accidentally shortened.
 
+### Pull transfer completion
+
+Every READ carries a native NIXL completion notification encoded as
+`request_id:expected_readers:transfers_from_this_reader`, so a reader sends one
+notification per transfer it issues, not one per request: a read split across
+memory types (a mixed DRAM/device read posts one READ per nonempty slice)
+produces one notification per READ. The `transfers_from_this_reader` field
+declares, in every notification from that reader, how many transfers it will
+issue for that producer. NIXL identifies the sending agent, so P counts
+notifications down separately for each reader and retires a reader only after
+its declared count has arrived. These counts can differ between readers: a
+reader with a single transfer declares one, while a reader with a fully local
+cache hit posts no READ at all and instead sends one immediate standalone
+acknowledgement with a transfer count of zero, which retires it right away.
+
+Topology determines how many readers (`expected_readers`) must finish before P
+may release the request's blocks. A mixed DRAM/device read attaches the same
+declared count to both transfer handles, so P can release its blocks only after
+both complete and every other expected reader has finished. Notification
+delivery does not require D to poll completion. If a split read only partially
+posts or completes, its missing notification keeps P's blocks retained until
+lease expiry; successful siblings do not authorize an early release.
+
+This wire format requires matching NIXL connector protocol versions on P and D.
+It does not establish pause/resume safety for queued reads, lease renewal, local
+receive postprocessing, or cache invalidation.
+
 ## Bidirectional KV Transfer
 
 For multi-turn conversations, [bidirectional KV transfer](../features/disagg_prefill.md) allows D to cache KV blocks that P can pull from on subsequent turns. Since the timing of the next conversational turn is **client-dependent** (not controlled by the system), the heartbeat-based lease mechanism does not apply here. Instead, a separate `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` (default 480s) provides a simple fixed timeout for blocks cached on D. If the client takes too long to continue the conversation, the blocks expire. D communicates back the expiry time so P can know when blocks are expired and recompute. Because the deadline is a `perf_counter` value produced on D and the two engines run in separate processes (with unrelated clocks), P estimates the clock offset to D from the handshake round-trip and applies it before comparing the deadline against its own `perf_counter`. Future work may extend a symmetric heartbeat mechanism to this case.

+

+    assert "req" not in worker._reqs_to_send
+
+

+    """A reader reporting more notifications than it declared must not be

inline_comments.body:
could you please elaborate on "each reader reports how many transfers
it needs for that producer."?
each reader will have only one notification per request, and for a fully local cache hit scenario, the completion request will be immediate, right.
inline_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -99,6 +99,27 @@ The heartbeat is deferred to the next step once the handshake completes --- the
 
 **On P (receiving):** In `_get_new_notifs()`, P's worker checks incoming NIXL notifications. Messages starting with `"HB:"` are routed to `_handle_heartbeat()`, which extends the lease expiry for each referenced request using `max(old_expiry, now + lease_extension)`. This ensures leases are never accidentally shortened.
 
+### Pull transfer completion
+
+Each READ carries a native NIXL completion notification encoded as
+`request_id:expected_readers:transfers_from_this_reader`. NIXL identifies the
+sending agent, so P counts completions separately for each reader. Topology
+determines how many readers must finish; each reader reports how many transfers
+it needs for that producer. These counts can differ between readers, for example
+when one has a local cache hit or only one nonempty memory-type slice.

inline_comments.body:
@snadampal thanks for reviewing! 
Yes, so the idea is that when we send the notif, we also send the number of xfer issued along.
So for a full prefix cache hit, we send a notif to release the block (like before), but specify 0 xfer were issued.
For a HiSparse xfer, we send 1 notification with num xfers 2, so P knows it is expecting 2 reads.
